title: KPZ Superdiffusion of Local Correlators in Diffusive Random Quantum Circuits
abstract: We study the single-particle Green's function $G(x,t)=\langle σ^-_x(0)σ^+_0(t)\rangle$ in one-dimensional particle-number-conserving random unitary circuits coupled to an external bath. For fixed spacetime disorder, we argue that $G(x,t)$ is governed, in both the strong- and weak-noise limits, by directed waves in a random medium. We find Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling in the wandering statistics of the normalized spatial distribution $p(x,t)\propto |G(x,t)|^2$ and in the associated free energy. In particular, its center $\langle x(t)\rangle\equiv\sum_x x\, p(x,t)$ wanders on a length-scale $\mathcal{O}(t^{2/3})$, while sample-to-sample fluctuations of $-\log\sum_x |G(x,t)|^2$ scale as $t^{1/3}$. At weak noise $γ\ll 1$, the crossover to the strong-disorder fixed point occurs at a parametrically long time $\mathcal{O}(γ^{-3/2})$. These predictions are confirmed numerically using tensor-network simulations of the noisy operator dynamics in individual circuits at moderate noise, and of a phase-annealed proxy retaining hopping disorder at weak noise.
summary: This work analyzes how quantum information decays in random unitary circuits by studying the single-particle Green's function. The authors find that this decay process exhibits universal Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling in certain limits. They develop sophisticated theoretical tools, including mapping to directed polymer models, to describe these non-equilibrium dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates the long-time dynamics of quantum coherence decay in random unitary circuits, contrasting standard hydrodynamic descriptions with non-equilibrium scaling laws.
main_result: The system exhibits Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling exponents in its wandering statistics in the strong noise limit, and a crossover to an effective directed polymer description in the weak noise limit.
method: The analysis employs mapping techniques, deriving effective continuum theories (like Directed Waves in Random Media or Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory actions), and utilizing tensor-network simulations for numerical confirmation.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional particle-number-conserving random unitary circuit coupled to an external bath. The dynamics are tracked via the single-particle Green's function G(x,t) and its associated spatial distribution p(x,t).
key_observables: Green's function G(x,t), normalized spatial distribution p(x,t), free energy fluctuations ($	ext{Var}[F(t)]$), and the center wandering $\langle x(t)angle$.
important_parameters: Noise parameter ($\gamma$), time ($t$), and length scales related to disorder strength.
main_assumptions: The strong-noise limit assumes collapse onto single-particle coherence, while the weak-noise analysis relies on projecting dynamics onto a source-manifold ansatz leading to an effective directed polymer description.
figures_summary: Figure 1 numerically confirms KPZ scaling exponents in TEBD simulations at moderate noise. Figure 2 shows variance collapse consistent with KPZ exponent 1/z = 2/3 for the weak-noise norm N.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the general Green's function dynamics, establishing KPZ scaling in the strong limit, to deriving a low-energy effective theory using phase averaging and Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory in the weak noise regime. It concludes by confirming that the final coarse-grained amplitude matches typical single-particle behavior.
why_interesting: The connection of quantum coherence decay in random circuits to universal scaling laws like KPZ is highly relevant for understanding decoherence mechanisms in disordered quantum systems, bridging condensed matter physics with non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
